title: 19 Threads statistics for 2026: Users, growth and engagement
content:
Since its record-breaking launch, Meta’s text-based network, Threads, has evolved from a viral phenomenon into a permanent fixture in the digital ecosystem. For marketing teams looking to build agile, multi-platform strategies this year, keeping a pulse on the latest social media statistics is non-negotiable.
What are Threads’ current performance metrics, and what does its trajectory look like heading into 2026? Threads has consistently built upon its initial growth milestones to secure a active user base. Beyond sheer volume, current engagement benchmarks point to a network where users are driving conversations rather than passively scrolling.
Whether you want to migrate audiences or build a net-new community, understanding these core metrics is essential to maximize your brand’s impact.
To understand the platform’s current standing, look at the foundational metrics defining its ecosystem. Analyzing these Threads platform statistics reveals how the network is transitioning from a viral novelty into a daily habit for millions.
Here is a scannable breakdown of the essential metrics highlighting Threads’ active user base, engagement health and global reach:
With Threads users continuing to climb, marketers can no longer rely on guesswork. Using Sprout Social’s Threads metrics and reporting features allows you to track performance across all your branded channels, enabling seamless, unified monitoring.
Threads’ growth from its initial launch to its current state is a masterclass in market penetration. While early user acquisition was largely driven by its frictionless Instagram Threads integration, sustained growth has been fueled by strategic feature rollouts and a broader industry shift toward text-based communities.
Tracking Threads monthly active users reveals an unprecedented growth velocity. After crossing the 275 million mark in Q3 2024, Threads reached 400 million MAUs in late 2025 . This quarter-over-quarter growth demonstrates that Threads successfully converted its initial novelty into a permanent daily habit.
For a full timeline of features that drove this growth, read more about what we learned about Meta Threads after its initial launch.
To appreciate the platform’s current scale, look at its viral launch. The network executed the most successful software launch in history by securing 30 million sign-ups in its first 24 hours . By day five, it shattered records by crossing 100 million users.
According to the Q2 2025 Consumer Pulse Survey, Threads has become sticky among newer platforms. Currently, about 14% of global social media users maintain a Threads profile. Looking at regional breakdowns, adoption sits at 14% across both US and UK while Australia tracks at 12%.
Following its viral launch, the platform’s installation rate maintained an impressive momentum globally. According to Statista , total worldwide app downloads for Threads hit 828 million by December 2025.
Generating over 72 million downloads in its launch month alone firmly established the app as a dominant force on mobile devices well before its first anniversary.
Threads initially launched in 100 countries, but was absent from the EU due to data protection regulations. However, the app saw a massive spike of over 34 million monthly downloads when it launched in the EU in December 2023.
Analyzing geographic distribution reveals a diverse global footprint. India dominates the global install base with a staggering 32% share of total downloads , while Brazil follows closely at 22%. The United States represents 16% of overall downloads.
The demographic segmentation of Threads heavily favors younger digital natives. Based on the Sprout Social Q2 2025 Consumer Pulse Survey, Gen Z and Millennials are the most active cohorts on the platform with each displaying a 17% adoption rate. They are followed by Gen X at 11% and Baby Boomers at 5%.
While the platform’s user base is diverse, male users account for 58% of the global audience on Threads, while female users make up the remaining 42%, according to Statista .
The platform’s growth trajectory remains strong heading into the future. According to the Q4 2025 Pulse Survey, 7% of social users plan to either start using Threads or increase their time spent on the app in 2026. Additionally, 3% of users are likely to use the networks as a dedicated channel to contact brands during the holiday season.
Monitoring daily user behavior patterns is the best way to determine actual platform health and establish reliable content performance benchmarks.
Threads has transitioned from a broadcast network into a deep conversational hub where active replies carry more weight than passive likes.
The evolution of Threads daily active users highlights incredible momentum. In October 2025, Adam Mosseri posted a Thread that the app’s total daily active users just passed 150 million .
Based on Threads’ previously reported 400 million MAUs, this 150 million DAU figure yields a stickiness ratio of roughly 37.5%. In the social media industry, a 20% to 50% ratio is generally considered a healthy baseline. This ratio proves Threads is successfully building strong, habitual engagement among its user base.
Unlike video-first platforms designed for infinite scrolling, Threads usage patterns are episodic. The average session length for Android users sits at 4 minutes .
Global football icon Neymar Jr. is the most-followed Threads account with 24.9 million followers, followed closely by Selena Gomez (20.7 million), Kylie Jenner (19 million) and Kim Kardashian (17 million).
Beyond celebrities, brands on Threads like Netflix and ClickUp are building massive reach potential through quick-witted, conversational posting strategies. Managing these high-volume conversations is seamless using Sprout Social’s Smart Inbox, ensuring no reply or brand mention goes unnoticed.
Threads is no longer an experimental channel. It’s a core pillar for modern community management that drives marketing investment and strategy shifts.
Early adoption is paying off for proactive companies. The Sprout Social Q1 2025 Marketer Pulse Survey shows that 57% of brands are already posting on Threads, with another 23% of marketers planning to build a presence on the network.
There is a distinct divide in industry adoption. According to the Q1 2025 Marketer Pulse Survey, 64% of B2C brands are posting on Threads compared to just 19% of B2B brands. However, B2B marketers recognize the opportunity and are catching up with 31% planning to establish a dedicated presence moving forward.
When it comes to content strategy, social teams are leaning on efficiency. The Q1 2025 Marketer Pulse Survey notes that 52% of marketers focus on repurposing existing content from other platforms to fuel their Threads presence, while 26% of brands plan to create entirely unique content for the app. Only 21% of brands plan to use a strategic mix of both approaches.
Brand content is resonating well on the platform. The 2026 Social Media Content Strategy Report highlights that about 30% of users typically engage with brand content on Threads at least once a week. This regular interaction emphasizes the importance of consistent posting cadence.
Users are receptive to quick hits of information. The same report shows that Threads users are most likely to interact with short-form video (under 60  seconds) and standard text posts. This is closely followed by user-generated and influencer content.
The 2026 Social Media Content Strategy Report reveals what users want from companies. When interacting with brands on Threads, 28% of users primarily want entertaining content. This is followed by sharing educational product content (15%), partnering with influencers (14%), providing customer service (14%) and promoting contests or giveaways (11%).
The ongoing rivalry between Threads and X (formerly Twitter) is a focal point for marketers. While both platforms cater to text-first microblogging, their competitive positioning and user behavior profiles have drastically diverged.
While X maintains a larger overall footprint with roughly 557 million monthly active users globally, Threads is quickly catching up.
Threads experienced a massive 127.8% year-over-year growth in mobile usage while X saw a 15.2% decline. However, X still dominates desktop traffic with over 145 million daily web visits compared to Threads’ 8.5 million.
Unlike other networks that rushed to monetize, Meta deliberately delayed ads to focus entirely on user retention and community building. Now, the platform is transitioning into a mature revenue-generating engine.
Financial analysts project that Threads could contribute $11.3 billion to Meta’s bottom line by 2026 . This revenue projection is intrinsically tied to the platform’s recent global advertising rollout. In early 2026, Meta opened its Threads ad inventory to all global advertisers allowing brands to deploy campaigns through Meta Ads Manager.
